subject: Multi-sprint capacity smoothing request & autoscale policy question
body:
From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai, emma@zephyrlabs.com
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Multi-sprint capacity smoothing request & autoscale policy question

Team —

Quick context: several high-priority pilots and internal infra worklines overlap across sprint 25–27 (May 2 — May 30). The attached sprint-capacity-matrix.xlsx maps out estimated GPU-hours per team. Early runs show a 45% overlap during the week of May 9 that will push our Dedicated pool close to capacity, which risks throttling some customer pilot traffic.

Ask: can product + infra approve a temporary "capacity smoothing" window that does two things for the date-range May 9–20:
- temporarily relax autoscale scale-up thresholds for Dedicated pool A (faster scale-up to 80% of burst lane)
- slow scale-down (increase cooldown from 2m -> 8m) to avoid oscillation when many short jobs land in parallel
- bind a soft quota per-team (soft limits that can be overridden by ops with justification)

Why this instead of carveouts/reservations: smoothing reduces cold-start churn and overall token-cost while avoiding permanent reservations for short multi-week sprints; it's cheaper and operationally lighter for everyone if we put guardrails in place.

Risks I'm worried about:
- increased cost for the period (~estimated +12k GPU-hours; see sheet)
- potential latency SLO impact for production traffic if burst lanes get saturated

Proposed mitigation:
- limit smoothing to weekday 08:00-20:00 PT; outside that window, normal autoscale rules apply
- require a short runbook for teams that want overrides (DevOps ticket with expected GPU-hours and business priority)
- set a hard emergency cutoff at 95% pool utilization that forces all non-prod jobs to queue

Please chime in with: (1) product approval, (2) infra feasibility (fast timeline? config changes), (3) finance/ops cost owner for tracking. I've attached autoscale-proposal-v1.md with the minimal kube/agent flags I'd change.

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
Senior Program Manager, Capacity Planning
Redwood Inference

Attachment: sprint-capacity-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)
Attachment: autoscale-proposal-v1.md (text)

---

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-sprint capacity smoothing request & autoscale policy question

Aditya —

Thanks for the clear summary and the sheet, appreciated. High-level thoughts from Product: we can support a temporary smoothing window subject to two conditions:
1) We get a short SLA/latency impact assessment from infra — need to know if 80% burst ramp could push p95 generation latency beyond our prod SLOs for the dedicated customers (especially Zephyr Labs).
2) Teams must tag all sprint jobs with cost-center metadata so Finance can attribute run-hours during the window. No free-for-all.

Questions:
- How many teams would be allowed to request override? Can we limit to three named projects for this window?
- If we approve slower scale-down, who owns potential cost overruns? Finance needs a named owner to approve the charge.

If infra confirms latency impact is minor, Product will sign off on the timebox and the weekday window you propose. Happy to escalate to Lauren for exec sign-off if Finance needs it.

-Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-sprint capacity smoothing request & autoscale policy question

Folks —

Infra feasibility notes:
- We can implement the two-config change (faster scale-up + longer cooldown) as feature flags at the autoscaler layer; low risk to rollout. I linked INFRA task: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-4321 for the change and testing job.
- We should be explicit about what "faster scale-up" means: propose to reduce the required pending queue time from 30s -> 10s and allow temporary burst to 80% of the burst lane for the named projects.
- We can also add an adaptive backpressure rule that kicks in if p95 latency > baseline + 25% for 3 consecutive minutes; that rule will block non-prod work.

Operational constraints:
- The Dedicated offering has a hard upper bound when nodes are fully provisioned in the region; if we hit node-provisioning limits from the cloud provider we'll need to fail open to a fallback model variant or pause non-prod. That provisioning latency can be 8–12 minutes at peak.
- Implementing a soft quota override flow requires a small UI change or a short Ops ticket template; I recommend the Ops ticket for this one-off.

Estimate timeline: we can implement flags in staging within 48 hours, test in canary (low-risk model) for 24 hours, and then flip to prod for the timebox if everything looks green.

I'll own the INFRA-4321 ticket and run the canary. Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Infra Reliability
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Multi-sprint capacity smoothing request & autoscale policy question

Quick note from Zephyr: our integration test campaign that week is fixed (we're bringing in a bunch of enterprise traffic May 11–14). If there are any forced pauses on non-prod the test could fail. We'd prefer to be considered a named project for override eligibility (we're happy to commit to tagging metadata and cost-center info).

Emma Hart
Head of Platform, Zephyr Labs
emma@zephyrlabs.com

Subject: Re: Multi-sprint capacity smoothing request & autoscale policy question

Thanks everyone — quick summary and actions: 
- Product: conditional approval granted assuming infra's adaptive backpressure rule prevents SLO regressions (Kim to confirm if exec sign-off required for cost owner).
- Infra: Marcus to own INFRA-4321; implement flags & canary timeline (48h -> 24h) and validation metrics.
- Ops/Finance: Lauren/Dev to confirm cost owner for the +12k GPU-hours window.
- External: Zephyr granted named override if they tag jobs and commit cost-center metadata.

Next steps (owners & ETA):
1) Marcus: push flags to staging and open canary run — ETA 2027-04-30 EOD.
2) Aditya: circulate final runbook and Ops ticket template — ETA 2027-04-30 noon.
3) Kimberly/Lauren: confirm cost owner and whether exec sign-off needed — ETA 2027-04-30 EOD.

If we get green on these by end of day Friday we'll flip the smoothing window for May 9–20.

- Aditya
